preamble: Retroflexion of the lateral [l] to [ɭ]. In the western and southern Indo-Aryan languages (Marathi, Gujarati, Odia, Rajasthani, Punjabi), single intervocalic Old Indo-Aryan -l- became retroflex -ḷ- [ɭ], while geminate -ll- stayed dental, so Sanskrit phala 'fruit' gives Marathi and Gujarati phaḷ and Odia phaḷa.

examples.note: Intervocalic single -l- of Old Indo-Aryan surfaces as the retroflex lateral ळ.
The learned doublet ફલ phal keeps dental [l].
